hints: Focus on how pressure affects a gas equilibrium, remember it shifts to the side with fewer gas molecules to reduce the pressure.
Count only the gas moles on each side for every equation, ignoring any solids completely.
Look for the one equation where the total number of gas moles on the right is smaller than on the left, so higher pressure pushes it right.
walkthrough:
**Recall Le Chatelier for pressure**

Increasing pressure makes the equilibrium shift to the side with the smaller number of moles of gas. This tries to lower the pressure again.

Rule: $\text{high pressure favours fewer gas moles}$

**Count gas moles only**

Solids do not count for pressure changes, only gases do. Let us list left vs right gas moles:

A: $0 \rightleftharpoons 1$, left 0, right 1

B: $4 + 1 = 5 \rightleftharpoons 2 + 2 = 4$, left 5, right 4

C: $2 \rightleftharpoons 1 + 1 = 2$, left 2, right 2

D: $4 \rightleftharpoons 4$, left 4, right 4

**Pick the shift to the right**

We want increased pressure to increase right-hand products, so we need fewer gas moles on the right than on the left. Only one equilibrium has $5$ gas moles going to $4$ gas moles, so pressure pushes it to the right.

options.A: Here $\text{CaCO}_3(\text{s}) \rightleftharpoons \text{CaO}(\text{s}) + \text{CO}_2(\text{g})$ has 0 gas moles on the left and 1 on the right. Increased pressure shifts to fewer gas moles, so to the left, decreasing the yield of products.
options.B: For $4\text{HCl}(\text{g}) + \text{O}_2(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{g}) + 2\text{Cl}_2(\text{g})$ there are 5 gas moles on the left and 4 on the right. Higher pressure favours the side with fewer gas moles, so the equilibrium moves right and product yield increases.
options.C: For $2\text{HI}(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons \text{H}_2(\text{g}) + \text{I}_2(\text{g})$ there are 2 gas moles on both sides. Pressure has no effect on the position, so yield is unchanged. A common trap is to count all molecules instead of comparing left and right.
options.D: For $3\text{Fe}(\text{s}) + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{g}) \rightleftharpoons \text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4(\text{s}) + 4\text{H}_2(\text{g})$ there are 4 gas moles on both sides. Pressure has no effect. The trap is to include the solids $\text{Fe}$ and $\text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4$ in the count, but only gases matter for pressure.
